source_definition.value: Self-distraction factor operationalized as a thought-suppression strategy: participants suppressed thoughts or feelings of anxiety or about the upcoming shock by quickly thinking of something else.

model_settings.value: Random-effects general linear model across 15 subjects; the four experimental conditions were modeled with phasic, tonic, and linearly increasing response profiles over each 15.6-second block, with pain events, megablock instructions, ratings, and six motion parameters included as regressors. Regressors were convolved with the canonical HRF; temporal high-pass filtering used a 128-second cutoff and temporal autocorrelations were corrected.

spans.text: In the present study, we therefore used a thought suppression paradigm to have subjects self-distract from anticipatory anxiety for pain while we recorded physiological (heart rate) and brain activity (by using functional magnetic resonance imaging [fMRI]).

description.value: Participants suppressed thoughts or feelings of anxiety or about the upcoming potential pain.

spans.text: Subjects were instructed to “suppress any thought or feeling of anxiety or about the shock.”
The Self-distraction factor was operationalized in” megablocks” that spanned eight blocks of anticipation/no anticipation.
At the end of a megablock, subjects indicated by a button press how much of the time after the instruction they had spent thinking about anxiety or pain or feeling anxiety

instructions.value: During high-pitch cue trials, participants were told that they might receive a painful electric stimulus to the hand with a probability of 25% during the following 15.6-second epoch. During low-pitch cue trials, they were told they would not be stimulated. In self-distraction blocks, they were instructed to suppress thoughts or feelings of anxiety or about the shock and, whenever an anxious thought or feeling or a thought about the shock arose, to quickly think of something else. In control blocks, they could think whatever they wanted but were not allowed to use the suppression strategy.

stimuli.value: High- or low-pitch double-beep cues signaled anticipation of possible painful electrical stimulation or safety, respectively. Pain stimuli were electrical pulse trains delivered to the back of the left or right hand at 25% probability during anticipation epochs.
